thread.title: Bank of America’s top Bay Area executive takes on new role

author: Mark Calvey
title: Bank of America’s top Bay Area executive takes on new role
text: – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Dec 7, 2018, 2:03pm PST Bank of America said this week that Thong Nguyen , a San Francisco-based executive who has been co-head of the consumer lines of business, will become vice chairman, focused on corporate strategy and payments. Charlotte-based BofA (NYSE: BAC) said that Dean Athanasia , Nguyen’s Boston-based counterpart overseeing consumer banking, will now become the sole head of the consumer lines, which include preferred, small business and retail banking, moving those responsibilities away from San Francisco. Nguyen’s move from the Charlotte headquarters to San Francisco in 2016 turned a lot of heads , given the huge role he played at the bank. Until this week, Nguyen was responsible for the operations of Bank of America’s coast-to-coast branch network, call centers, ATM network and the digital banking operations, with more than 36 million active users, according to the bank’s website Friday. Nguyen’s team was responsible for serving the bank’s 67 million consumer and small business customers. At the time of Nguyen’s move to San Francisco, CEO Brian Moynihan said in a statement, “Thong’s background and his current responsibilities will serve us well in harnessing the creative power of this unique market and in sharpening our capabilities to help improve the financial lives of our clients.” In a 2016 interview with the San Francisco Business Times, Nguyen said, "I work best behind the scenes, helping to make things happen. My only measure of success will be whether this engine continues to run without me." Other moves Bank of America also said this week that small business banking regional executive Emily Shanks will retire at the end of the month . Her successor, Roger Forman , is based in Seattle and plans to split his time between San Francisco and Seattle. Shanks, as a division sales executive for BofA’s small business banking national sales team, is responsible for the bank’s Northwest division that runs from Northern California up through Washington state. Shanks is based in Concord and for a time served as BofA’s market president for the East Bay. In August, California’s largest bank named Gioia McCarthy as market president for both San Francisco and the East Bay, serving as the public face of the bank in the local community. McCarthy came to San Francisco from the bank’s operations in Southern California about two years ago. Bank of America said the Bay Area continues to be a “priority market” for the bank, which employs 5,800 people and operates 211 branches in the region. The bank has also made some key hires in the Bay Area for its digital banking leadership team . BofA has hired Tommy Elliott from Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) as digital payments executive, based in Sunnyvale and San Francisco; Rachel Kobetz came over from Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) as head of design, based in San Francisco; and Nikki Katz joined from the Walt Disney Co. (NYSE: DIS) to be BofA’s digital strategy and transformation executive, based in Los Angeles. Brent Reston , BofA’s head of digital sales, is also based in San Francisco. BofA said Friday that Nguyen’s continued presence in San Francisco is a sign of the importance the bank places on the region. “Thong has been elevated to vice chairman and his role expanded to lead some of our most important strategic initiatives, including enterprise payments and corporate initiatives critical to accelerating responsible growth as we move forward,” said BofA spokeswoman Betty Riess , based in San Francisco. “The importance of San Francisco/Silicon Valley is a key reason why he’s based here and his continued presence in San Francisco reinforces the bank’s commitment to the West Coast.” – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Dec 7, 2018, 2:03pm PST Related Content
